attempts.summary: Built a MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch on node1/node2/node3 (Ubuntu 16.04 i386), then added node4 as a fourth member carrying existing application data and accepting writes. Ubuntu's native mariadb-server-10.0 package on this i386 image lacks wsrep/Galera support (confirmed: "unknown variable 'wsrep_on'"), so switched to the official MariaDB 10.1 i386 repo, which does include full wsrep support (104 wsrep options found via mysqld --help --verbose). node1 was bootstrapped as the founding cluster member with an appdb.orders table and seed rows; node2 and node3 joined via automatic rsync SST and replicated the existing data; node4 was installed identically, its config fixed to load from the correct conf.d path (its fresh install lacked the mariadb.conf.d include used by the others), and joined the running cluster, receiving the same data via SST. Cross-node writes from node3 and node4 confirmed multi-master replication to all peers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on each node, restarted each of the 4 nodes one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (never more than one down at once, quorum preserved throughout since only 1 of 4 was ever offline), confirmed each node's boot_id changed post-restart, and verified mysql auto-started (SysV rc2.d symlinks) with wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_size=4, and all application data intact. Final end-to-end write/read check across nodes confirms the 4-member cluster is healthy and consistent.
